title: Blank defined by the next sentence or after a colon
subtitle: Words in Context · 55 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **55 of the official questions in Words in Context are this one** — 33 Easy, 14 Medium, 8 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- A blank sits in one sentence, and the next sentence begins with an example marker (such as 'for example') or follows a colon or dash.
- That second part describes concretely what the blank means.
- The blank is usually a noun or adjective that sums up that description.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Skip the blank and read the explanation or example that follows it.
- 2) Write down a one-word summary of what it shows.
- 3) Choose the option that matches your summary most exactly, not just in general tone.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You choose a word that is on topic, or that suits the subject in general, but does not name what the example actually shows.
For instance, you pick a positive word when the evidence points to one specific quality, such as precision.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You choose a word that is on topic, or that suits the subject in general, but does not name what the example actually shows.
For instance, you pick a positive word when the evidence points to one specific quality, such as precision.
